Attribution: Nieman Reports [media_lens] https://niemanreports.org/local-news-detroit-michigan-public-media-sarah-alvarez-founder-ceo-community-needs-foreclosures-outlier-media-documenters-city-bureau-chicago/

Sarah Alvarez has spent much of her career rethinking how local journalism can serve the public. After working as a civil rights attorney, then as a reporter and producer at the NPR station Michigan Public, she founded Outlier Media in 2016. Alvarez said the Detroit-based nonprofit newsroom was designed to fill information and accountability gaps in communities that were often overlooked by traditional news organizations.. One of its signature innovations, TXT OUTLIER, is a text message service Alvarez created to connect Detroiters directly with journalists and provide practical information on issues affecting their lives, from utility bills to housing and foreclosures. Under Alvarez’s leadership, Outlier also expanded its Documenters program, an initiative that trains and pays residents to attend and report on public meetings to create a public record of local government decisions in places that don’t have press coverage. The initiative has engaged more than 700 Detroiters and since spread nationwide, creating new opportunities for civic participation and public accountability.

With the first U.S. midterm elections since President Donald Trump’s return to the White House approaching, voters will be weighing in on a range of issues, from the economy and rising cost of living, to the administration’s foreign policy and the future direction of both major parties. At a recent virtual Nieman-to-Nieman seminar, a group of Nieman alums who cover politics discussed what they’re hearing from voters with regards to key Senate races, the growing influence of younger voters drawn to progressive candidates, and the political implications of conflicts involving Iran, Ukraine, and Russia. Moderated by Austin Bogues (NF ’21), news desk editor at USA Today, the discussion brought together James Barragán (NF ’24), political anchor for Spectrum News in Austin, Texas; Bill Barrow (NF ’22), national politics reporter for The Associated Press in Atlanta; and Ines Pohl (NF ’05), Washington bureau chief and White House correspondent for Deutsche Welle, Germany’s international public broadcaster.

As protests continue across India over allegations of government corruption, dozens of members of the media have been subjected to arrest, detainment and assault, according to witnesses, press rights organizations, and the journalists themselves. Thousands of protesters have taken to the streets of New Delhi in recent weeks, demanding the resignation of election officials allegedly tied to the deletion of nearly 130 million names from voter registration rolls. The protests — which have largely been organized by the Cockroach Janata Party, so named after India's chief justice called the nation’s unemployed youth and activists "cockroaches" — are part of a wider wave of youth discontent aimed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his administration. Organizers have mobilized young people via social media, tapping into frustrations with government corruption, eroding trust in democratic institutions, and a lack of access to jobs and educational opportunities.

The Trump administration’s latest attacks on the news media have followed a familiar pattern: President Donald Trump lashes out at news outlets for perceived bias and follows up with restrictive actions that appear blatantly unconstitutional; a judge’s ruling follows, temporarily halting the actions; and the administration pivots and pushes ahead with other restrictions. This time it was the removal of three outlets — CNN, MS NOW, and Politico — from White House press access in September. After the groups sued, and U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly issued a temporary restraining order restoring their access on Sept. 24, the administration barred CNN and Politico from providing pool coverage on trips outside Washington. Kelly issued a longer, preliminary injunction on Oct. 14, halting the administration from blocking the news organizations’ access to the White House while the case proceeds. ### This Newsroom Wants You to Be Part of the Journey Before It Even Starts
Source: Nieman Reports
Published: 2026-10-06 10:00 UTC
URL: https://niemanreports.org/independent-journalism-new-newsroom-launch-otter-news-daniel-drepper-business-plan-climate-crisis-environmental-journalism/
Source meta: reference_tool · aggregator · R3 · P4 · reference

Attribution: Nieman Reports [media_lens] https://niemanreports.org/independent-journalism-new-newsroom-launch-otter-news-daniel-drepper-business-plan-climate-crisis-environmental-journalism/

My happiest times in journalism have been when I have built something new. For my latest venture, I want to help bring investigative journalism on climate and environmental issues to a much larger audience than it has reached in the past. To do so, I’m starting a brand-new newsroom focused on the environmental and climate crisis, and I’m taking my audience along for the ride. I’ll be documenting every facet of the process with an “open kitchen” approach of radical transparency, starting with a 100-day video countdown chronicling all the steps involved with starting a news organization from the ground up. This effort combines two of the things I’m most passionate about: I love digging up stories that other people don’t want to see published, and I love creating opportunities for other journalists. I’ve been a journalist for most of my life. I started working at age 14 for the local paper in my rural German town, turned to doing investigative stories in my early 20s, and later studied investigative journalism at the Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism in New York.

### America’s Shrinking Local Newsrooms, Through a Photographer’s Lens
Source: Nieman Reports
Published: 2026-10-02 12:30 UTC
URL: https://niemanreports.org/americas-shrinking-local-newsrooms-photographer-ann-hermes-local-news-news-deserts-rural-america/
Source meta: reference_tool · aggregator · R3 · P4 · reference
Fetched: 2026-11-20 01:35 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Nieman Reports [media_lens] https://niemanreports.org/americas-shrinking-local-newsrooms-photographer-ann-hermes-local-news-news-deserts-rural-america/

For many journalists, the sight of empty desks is a sadly familiar one. My first glimpse of a gutted newsroom facing further cutbacks sparked a documentary photography project that has so far taken me to more than 50 newsrooms across the United States over the past eight years. It began when my mother, a loyal subscriber to our local metro in southern Illinois, told me a decade ago how disappointed she was in the newspaper. She complained that the local coverage was lacking, and the paper seemed to be thinner. Already several years into my photojournalism career, I was unsurprised by her remarks — I had been witnessing the decline of print media since graduation from journalism school. Still, my curiosity was piqued, and I arranged a visit to the paper to see for myself. Cue the scene of a barren newsroom. Not only were there empty desks, but also an expanse of exposed carpet with indentations showing where desks had once long stood. While there has been a great deal of reporting on the issues plaguing local journalism, I hadn’t seen the story told visually.

### 澳枪击事件嫌疑人为父子：曾宣誓效忠“伊斯兰国”，行凶枪支为合法持有
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-16 02:23 UTC
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178049
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-20 01:35 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178049

据新华社12月15日援引澳大利亚广播公司报道，澳大利亚联合反恐小组调查人员表示，悉尼邦迪滩枪击事件两名嫌疑人曾宣誓效忠“伊斯兰国”恐怖组织。 报道援引联合反恐小组一名不愿透露姓名的高级官员的话说，警方在邦迪滩两名枪手车内发现一面“伊斯兰国”旗帜。澳大利亚安全情报组织6年前就已在调查邦迪滩枪击案两名枪手之一的纳维德·阿克拉姆，他与“伊斯兰国”在悉尼的恐怖分子有密切联系。 澳大利亚警方表示，枪击事件的两名嫌疑人是父子关系，使用合法获得的枪支发动了此次袭击事件。 澳大利亚总理阿尔巴尼斯15日表示：“今天下午4点， 我将把更严格的枪支法律列入国家内阁的议程，包括限制个人可持有或许可的枪支数量 。此外，还需对许可证进行定期审查。人们的情况会发生变化，人们的思想也会随着时间的推移而变得激进。许可证不应永久有效。” 此次枪击事件已造成包括1名作案嫌疑人在内的16人死亡、40人受伤。这是自1996年塔斯马尼亚州亚瑟港枪击事件造成35人死亡以来，澳大利亚发生的最严重的大规模枪击事件。 持有枪支许可证长达十年 据多家外媒报道，其中一名袭击者为24岁的澳大利亚公民纳维德·阿克拉姆，他在现场被捕，随后被送往悉尼的一家医院。另一名袭击者是他的父亲萨吉德·阿克拉姆，他于1998年来到澳大利亚，被警方当场击毙。 澳大利亚警方随后证实，纳维德·阿克拉姆此前已被新南威尔士州警方和其他机构记录在案。其父亲萨吉德·阿克拉姆持有枪支许可证，名下登记有6支枪，目前均已被追回。新南威尔士州警察局长马尔·兰永透露，萨吉德·阿克拉姆已持有枪支许可证长达十年。 阿尔巴尼斯在新闻发布会上透露，纳维德·阿克拉姆曾于2019年10月首次引起当局的注意。他补充说，对该男子进行检查是基于他与其他人有联系，但评估结果表明，没有任何迹象表明他存在持续的威胁或暴力倾向。 新南威尔士州州长克里斯·明斯表示，警方正在调查他们的系统是否存在故障，导致合法持有的武器可能被用于恐怖袭击。 枪手“性格古怪”，爱好打猎 据《卫报》澳大利亚版报道，纳维德·阿克拉姆在袭击前从事砌砖工作。他的同事表示，纳维德性格古怪，“没人和他亲近”。“（砌砖工人）在一起的时间很长，因为砌砖是一项非常枯燥乏味的工作，所以大家会聊很多话。但纳维德是一个性格很古怪的人……他工作非常努力，几乎没有休息日。” 尽管澳大利亚警方并未确认纳维德·阿克拉姆是否合法持有枪支，但据这位同事表示，纳维德经常外出打猎，曾提及在昆士兰州南部高原的克鲁克韦尔附近射杀兔子和其他猎物。这位同事还表示，就在几周前，纳维德告诉老板，他的手骨折了，所以要到2026年才能工作。

在校园里，孩子们时常举起戴在手腕上的手表，彼此一碰，便加为好友。 这种以“安全”为核心卖点的儿童电话手表，如今已超越通信工具的属性，悄然演变成一个拥有独特规则、社交层级甚至灰色产业链的未成年人数字社交圈——“小天才圈”。 在这个属于他们的“江湖”里，“大佬榜”备受关注，“扩列”（增加好友）成为新的社交需求，“点主”（在主页点赞）是每日必做的功课……这些让成年人感到陌生的词汇，正构筑着未成年人的数字社交世界。 然而，伴随着这种社交形态的兴起，家长们的担忧也日益加剧：孩子过度沉迷手表社交、不良信息传播、因品牌壁垒导致的“社交绑架”等问题逐渐浮现。《法治日报》记者近日对该现象展开调查，试图揭开这一未成年人数字社交圈的真实面貌。 点赞成社交“硬通货” 据北京“小天才圈”资深玩家陈曦（化名）介绍，圈内有5000余名活跃用户，多为11岁至17岁的学生，这个社交圈形成了一套精心设计的“混圈规则”。“入圈”需设定两个字的独特圈名，随后可在平台分享生活点滴，吸引具有相同爱好的好友进行互动；若想提升知名度或影响力，需每日经营主页并与好友动态互动。 记者注意到，在一些社交平台上，大量以“小天才圈交友攻略”为主题的内容应运而生，内容涵盖如何快速“扩列”、获取更多点赞等“实用”技巧，评论区有不少“留下ID互加好友”的留言。在这一社交体系中，点赞是这套规则的核心——平台设定每日主页获赞上限为3000个，若要达到“100万+”的“大佬”级别，需连续点赞近一年时间。围绕点赞数与知名度，圈内形成了清晰的“大佬排行榜”，点赞数也成为社交“硬通货”。 这种对点赞的追逐，已催生出相关服务产业。记者调查发现，某社交平台上，拥有数十万甚至上百万点赞数的账号，售价从几百元到上千元不等：100多万点赞的账号标价1300元，90多万点赞的账号标价1200元。 今年18岁的“灵师”（圈名），在2021年14岁时加入“小天才圈”，她的账号目前已拥有150个好友、超100万点赞量。她告诉记者，这样的账号市场价值约1000元。 “围绕点赞需求，还衍生出代刷赞、租账号、出售‘大佬好友位’等服务。”“灵师”进一步介绍，例如付费100元至180元，即可获得“bot”（记者注：“bot”是一种第三方开发的自动化工具，主要用于刷赞、修改记录和发送动态等功能，这类工具能帮助用户快速提升账号点赞数，从而在未成年人社交圈中获得更高地位）自动点赞功能——用户将手表寄给相关人员进行10天左右的处理便能完成安装。此后，发帖5分钟内即可自动获赞，还可以一键查询未点赞名单。

### 产地造假、年份速成、无视监管！央视曝光新会陈皮市场乱象
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-15 08:23 UTC
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32176166
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline

Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32176166

近日，总台接到群众举报，反映陈皮市场存在年份虚标、产地及工艺造假等问题，千元一斤的“年份陈皮”亦可能名不副实。 茶枝柑新果皮冒充陈皮 广西浦北出现“速成工艺陈皮” 记者发现，直播间里售卖陈皮低价轮番轰炸，年份承诺掷地有声。 直播间也有主播爆料，八成市面上所谓广东新会陈皮实为广西陈皮。 广西钦州市浦北县是茶枝柑重要种植基地，其果皮是陈皮风味“越陈越香”关键，也是浦北陈皮唯一原料。2024年当地陈皮产业产值破60亿元，采收季大量鲜果加工晾晒成柑皮。 果农和收购商称，今年浦北茶枝柑鲜果收购价走低。按20斤鲜果出1斤柑皮比例，叠加人工成本，品相好的新柑皮成本约30元/斤，低端柑皮仅六七元，且当年新柑皮并非真正陈皮。 这家企业的负责人告诉记者，按行业共识与团体标准，柑皮需陈化三年以上才可称为陈皮，陈化时间越长价值越高，但他透露，自然陈化需长期积压资金，多数企业是难以承受的。 这家企业的负责人私下告诉记者，为缓解资金占用压力，一种名为“轻工艺”的速成加工方式，眼下正在部分陈皮生产企业里流行，他们仅需一个月的时间，就能将新采收的茶枝柑果皮处理为外观近似三年、五年自然陈化过的陈皮，这样做能大幅缩短陈化周期、降低企业的运营成本。 浦北自然陈化五年陈皮批发价每斤150元至200元，企业造假“工艺皮”成本仅70元左右，高额利润促使更多商家放弃自然陈化、铤而走险。 记者离开企业，在广西浦北县柑浦堂健康产业有限公司分拣车间，再次见到大批量造假“工艺皮”陈皮，同一批“工艺皮”因加工受热差异形成色差，被分拣标注为三年、五年等不同年份。 负责人透露，不同年份“工艺皮”本质相同，批发价均70元左右一斤，零售价差极大，标五年款卖500元一斤，标十年款卖1000元一斤，仅凭外观就能翻倍抬价，利润超成本十倍以上。 新会陈皮从浦北进货 “工艺皮”贴上陈皮标签以假乱真 浦北与新会陈皮原料同为茶枝柑，仅产地不同，新会较高生产成本使当地部分头部商家常年从浦北拿货，浦北成其重要原料供应地。 记者在柑浦堂分拣仓库看到，大量标注“新会陈皮”“新会特产”的纸箱正打包“工艺皮”，这些广西陈皮每日批量发往广东新会，造假供需链路已成熟稳定。 记者发现，浦北当地部分规模企业和小型收购商，已形成了这种“工艺皮”的造假供应体系，可自主加工或快速调配各类“年份”陈皮货品，个别企业年销新会原料数量惊人。 随后经浦北陈皮企业负责人引荐，记者见到多位专程从新会赴浦北采购的商家，他们坦言同时经营新会皮与浦北皮，外地“工艺皮”因价格低廉成电商供货重要选择。

### 《怦然心动》导演莱纳与妻子在家中遇害，警方尚未证实是其子所杀

当地时间12月14日，曾执导《怦然心动》《当哈利遇到莎莉》《危情十日》等影片的美国导演罗伯·莱纳（Rob Reiner）在他位于洛杉矶的家中遇害身亡。洛杉矶警察已对外证实，现年78岁的莱纳与他现年68岁的妻子米歇尔·辛格·莱纳（Michele Singer Reiner）的遗体一同被发现。 2019年，罗伯·莱纳（左一）与《当哈利遇到莎莉》的主演梅格·瑞恩、比利·克里斯托出席TMC经典电影节。 据悉，洛杉矶消防局的人员于当地时间12月14日下午3点38分接到医疗救助电话，赶赴位于布伦特伍德区的一处住宅中，随后发现两人已死亡。当天晚间，洛杉矶警察局在其社交媒体官方账号确认死者为导演罗伯·莱纳夫妇，将由抢劫凶杀部门主导调查。而好莱坞媒体TMZ援引执法部门消息称，“两人身上有与刀具造成的伤口相符的割裂伤。” 好莱坞媒体《每日野兽》称，有消息人士向他们透露，是两人的女儿罗米最先发现他们倒在血泊中；罗伯·莱纳当时已死亡，妻子米歇尔在救护车送院途中离世。 此外，《人物》杂志称通过多方消息，得知莱纳夫妇系被他们的儿子尼克（Nick）所杀害。不过，这一说法并未获得警方的证实。罗伯·莱纳与摄影师米歇尔·辛格相识于《当哈利遇到莎莉》拍摄时期，两人于1989 年结婚，育有三个子女，分别为杰克（Jake）、尼克（Nick）和罗米（Romy）。 2014年，罗伯·莱纳与妻子偕三名子女杰克、罗米、尼克（右三至右一）出席活动。 《人物》杂志还在报道中指出：尼克2016年接受其采访时，曾谈到自己长达数年的毒品成瘾经历。这段经历始于他十几岁出头，导致他一度流落街头。他表示，大约从15岁开始，便反复进出戒毒康复机构；随着成瘾问题不断加重，他逐渐与家人疏远，并在多个州经历了长时间的无家可归生活。 2025年9月15日，罗伯·莱纳在纽约出席活动。视觉中国 图 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

### 演员何晴追悼会举行，其子追思母亲：北京这场雪像是为她而下

Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline

Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178536

一场雪落，人间倩影化雪归天。 12月15日上午，众多剧迷粉丝冒着严寒赶到北京昌平殡仪馆久安厅，送别演员何晴最后一程。12月13日，这位被誉为“古典第一美人”的演员因病去世，终年61岁。 不到10点，殡仪馆告别厅外已经站满了前来悼念的观众和粉丝，有人胸前佩戴小白花，有人手捧鲜花，一位浙江的网友还托人送来了悼念花圈。 “何晴的作品在我们心中留下了太多美好回忆，她的演技和性格都让我们深深喜爱，这次听到她突然去世的消息，我们非常意外，来到这里也是一种悼念。”一位何晴的影迷说。 现场粉丝在悼念簿上写下对何晴的话，不到一会儿，悼念簿就已写满对她的怀念。一位观众用清秀的字迹写下：“亲爱的何晴，我们的童年、青春都在您的影视作品中得到陪伴。美丽可人的何晴，很痛心听到您的消息，我代表我的同学们来这为你送行。” 曾在电视剧《水浒传》中饰演卢俊义的演员王卫国也来到现场，神色哀切。他说自己和何晴既是邻居，也是多年好友，在他印象中何晴是一个温婉、暖心的人，没有架子，总是远远地和人打招，笑嘻嘻地说话。何晴生病时常给王卫国打电话，请他送自己去医院。即便病重时，何晴也保持乐观积极的态度，王卫国有些事情想不开，她还来开导自己。“何晴走了，我们都很难过。只要你记住她，她就永远还在。”王卫国说。 《水浒传》中卢俊义的扮演者王卫国 《西游记》中万圣公主扮演者张青深情回忆何晴往事：“我们是小时候就认识的好朋友，从80年代到现在，有缘分做了这些年的朋友。她说话慢慢的，很甜很温柔。” 《西游记》中万圣公主扮演者张青 在广大观众的真挚请求下，原本仅面向亲友的告别仪式临时对外开放，大家排着队，秩序井然地进入灵堂，与这位“荧屏中的温婉佳人、生活中的坚韧女性”做最后的道别。 久安厅内的屏幕上滚动播放着何晴的照片，厅内四周摆满了亲友的花圈，其中包括六小龄童、唐国强、翁虹、尤勇智等何晴圈内好友送来的花圈，还有《三国演义》剧组送来的花圈。人群中不时传来一阵抽泣。 何晴之子许何代表亲友致悼词。他回忆了何晴对抗病魔的乐观积极，以及作为母亲对孩子深深的爱和眷恋。 许何说，妈妈很喜欢下雪，经常在雪后穿一件毛茸茸的衣服外出赏雪。“今年12月12日北京下了第一场雪，我摸着妈妈的脸跟她说北京下雪了，下得好大，好像很久都没有下过这么大的雪。在我的心里，这场雪好像是刻意为她下的。12月13日早晨天空晴朗，白色的雪布满了大地，我妈妈在她最喜欢的早晨离开了大家，去了天国，远离了所有的疾病和痛苦。” 何晴，1964年1月13日出生于浙江衢州江山市。她是中国内地唯一一位演遍四大名著影视作品的女演员，被誉为“古典第一美女”。

Click to expand Image People gather outside the International Court of Justice following the landmark ruling that found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya, The Hague, November 19, 2026. © 2026 Human Rights Watch (The Hague) – The International Court of Justice’s (ICJ) landmark ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya is a historic milestone in their long quest for justice, Human Rights Watch said today. On November 19, 2026, the ICJ found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya during the 2016-2017 “clearance operations,” carried out by Myanmar’s military. In the case brought by Gambia against Myanmar for alleged violations of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide (Genocide Convention), the court ruled for Gambia, with a nine to six vote by the judges, that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. This is the first time that the ICJ found a country responsible for committing genocide.

Click to expand Image Bahraini human rights activist Nabeel Rajab arrives for his appeal hearing at court in Manama, February 11, 2015. © 2015 Hamad I Mohammed/Reuters (New York) – Nabeel Rajab, a prominent human rights activist from Bahrain and a close partner of Human Rights Watch, passed away on November 17, 2026, at the age of 62. He reportedly died in Türkiye following a heart attack. Rajab rose to prominence as a human rights defender in Bahrain in the 1990s, and in 2000 he co-founded the Bahrain Human Rights Society, one of Bahrain’s first human rights organizations. He then co-founded the Bahrain Centre for Human Rights in 2002, later becoming its president, and co-founded and was executive director of the Gulf Centre for Human Rights starting in 2011. Rajab had served as a member of the Human Rights Watch Middle East and North Africa division’s advisory committee since 2010, playing a key role not only in supporting Human Rights Watch work in Bahrain, but also providing guidance to the documentation and advocacy work that Human Rights Watch carries out across the region.

Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/worker-runs-how-compensation-design-can-curb-contagious-departures-weil-gotschal

The proposed dissolution of Weil, Gotshal & Manges followed an exodus of prominent partners from one of America’s largest law firms. Its rapid decline illustrates how departures by key employees can encourage others to leave, even when a firm remains profitable. This column explains why such departures can become self-reinforcing and how firms can mitigate the problem through compensation design. Deferred fixed pay, dilutable compensation, and different compensation structures across employees can help firms retain skilled teams at lower cost.

Source: CEPR VoxEU

Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline

Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/return-inflation-more-bank-profits-more-central-bank-losses

Central banks use the interest rate paid on reserves as their key monetary policy instrument. This column argues that monetary policy creates an important cycle in banks’ profitability. Since 2021, return on equity and net interest income in euro area banks have increased, following higher interest rates and the previous quantitative easing programme. The counterpart to this development is large losses at central banks and a burden on taxpayers in the Eurosystem. To deal with this, it suggests central banks increase the unremunerated minimum reserves or to consider a tax on banks’ excess profits.

Europe’s competitiveness debate has renewed calls to give greater weight to scale, investment, and efficiencies in merger policy. This column presents evidence from mergers reviewed by the European Commission between 1990 and 2024. On average, markups and profits rise following mergers, while citation-weighted patenting falls for both merging firms and their rivals. The responses of rival firms are particularly informative for distinguishing firm-specific rationalisation from a broader weakening of competitive pressure.

### The health costs of organised crime
Source: CEPR VoxEU
Published: 2026-11-19 00:00 UTC
URL: https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/health-costs-organised-crime
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/health-costs-organised-crime

Organised crime can impose costs that extend well beyond violence, market distortions, and weakened institutions. This column presents evidence on the long-run health consequences of illegal toxic-waste disposal in Southern Italy. Comparing municipalities similarly close to illegal disposal sites but differentially exposed because of historical wind patterns shows large and persistent effects on the number of cancer deaths in downwind municipalities. Consistent with epidemiological evidence on dioxin exposure, these effects emerge only after long latencies. Effects are particularly pronounced on deaths from all causes among younger age groups.

Geopolitical tensions are changing the nature of supply-chain risk. This column presents new survey evidence showing that EU firms increasingly regard trade disruptions as persistent but are moving away from emergency responses such as stockpiling towards longer-term diversification of suppliers and markets. The EU Single Market provides an important buffer against external shocks. At the same time, experimental evidence shows that geopolitical disruptions can have sizeable and asymmetric effects on firms' investment.

### How Will the 340B Rebate Model Pilot Affect Covered Entity Finances? -- by Charles J. Courtemanche
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36006#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-20 01:35 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36006#fromrss

The Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) plans to implement a pilot switching 340B from an upfront discount model to a rebate model for drugs in the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program (MDPNP). This study uses calibration methods to predict the impact of the rebate model pilot (RMP) on covered entities’ net revenues from the 340B program. I examine possible losses from averted duplicate discounts; denial of valid claims; manufacturers using data to exert influence; liquidity-related expenses; and administrative and staffing costs. I also project the effects of switching the entire 340B program to a rebate model. I project net revenue losses from the RMP of $1.5 billion. Expansion to all of 340B would increase the predicted losses to $22.8 billion, cutting net revenues from the program by 32%. The majority of losses will come from administrative and staffing costs, which do not benefit manufacturers, implying a net negative effect of switching to a rebate model.

### Horizontal Equity of Taxation: Citizen Beliefs and Policy Preferences -- by Pierre Bachas, Christopher A. Hoy, Anders Jensen, Mahvish Shaukat
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36007#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-20 01:35 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36007#fromrss

Taxes are harder to enforce on the self-employed than on wage earners, creating horizontal inequities among taxpayers with similar incomes. Using tax microsimulation and household survey data from 29 developing countries, we show that horizontal inequities in actual tax systems are comparable in magnitude to vertical equity and are exacerbated by progressive reforms that fall disproportionately on wage earners. We then conduct surveys and randomized information experiments in Pakistan to study public perceptions of these inequities. Although providing information raises fairness concerns, it does not increase support for reforms reducing it, revealing an important political constraint to improving tax equity.

### Monetary policy in a Phelps–Winter Economy -- by Bruce C. Greenwald, Joseph E. Stiglitz
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36008#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-20 01:35 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36008#fromrss

We use the Phelps-Winter customer market—providing a better theory of price determination for large parts of the economy than the standard model—to show that raising interest rates induces higher prices, as firms value current profits more, and are more willing to lose customers for short-term gains. These inflationary effects can be significant in relevant ranges of interest rates; they exist in the short run even when interest rate hikes succeed in cutting aggregate demand; and that they are amplified by policy uncertainty and the uncertainty about the effects of interest rate changes, both of which have increased as conventional policy has demonstrably failed badly to keep inflation at the 2% target. Empirical studies confirm this low level of ineffectiveness of raising interest rates in reducing inflation.

Impact measurement is central to impact investing and social entrepreneurship, yet little is known about whether firms benefit privately from measuring impact. We conduct the first randomized controlled trial of an impact measurement intervention among high-growth social enterprises in India. Treated firms exhibit nearly twice as much revenue growth and raise nearly twice as much capital as control firms. In a companion experiment with early-stage investors, we find that investors respond strongly to quantified impact metrics but not to generic qualitative impact statements. Together, our results show that impact measurement can shape firm growth and capital allocation.

### Gambling for Goals -- by Costas Arkolakis, Spencer Y. Kwon, Dominic Russel, Claire Shi, Hyunjoo Yang
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36010#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-20 01:35 UTC

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36010#fromrss

Young adults in advanced economies have grown more pessimistic about their economic prospects in recent years. At the same time, gambling-like financial activities have proliferated. We link these trends through a Friedman-Savage (1948) motive: when life goals such as homeownership or marriage seem out of reach, individuals turn to financial gambles. We test this theory using an original survey combined with millions of linked records from Korea’s leading credit bureau, telecom provider, and credit card issuer. Consistent with the theory, individuals who place greater importance on hard-to-reach goals take more risk, and the form of risk they take varies systematically with their distance from those goals. Within individuals, cryptocurrency app usage rises during unemployment and falls after winning the right to purchase price-regulated housing through a lottery. A calibration shows how hard-to-reach goals lead households to act more aggressively on their beliefs, amplifying the consequences of overoptimism.

### Investment and Governance: Through The Lens of Sustainability -- by Jitendra Aswani, Roberto Rigobon

Using 3,944 sustainable bond issuances by public firms from 2013 to 2022, we examine the causal effect of sustainable investment on governance adoption. A heteroskedasticity-based identification strategy reveals that a 1% increase in sustainable debt (by total debt) raises the likelihood of sustainable governance adoption by 9.2%. Such adoption improves environmental performance by 16% (structural estimates). These effects are confined to non-financial firms; for financial firms, governance adoption alone is in-sufficient, as sustainable loan borrowers environmental performance does not improve. Firms with stronger environmental performance are less likely to adopt sustainable governance. Results are robust to alternative definitions and extensive specification checks.

Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is AI building successive, more capable iterations of itself. As the race to build superintelligent AI speeds up, RSI is a natural way for more powerful AI to be built and trained. Frontier labs already use AI extensively to build their future models. For instance, the chart below shows the share of experiments AI can handle, with experiments that are fully automatable by AI on the far right. Figure 1. AI automation of R&D at Anthropic RSI Risks RSI lets labs develop capabilities faster, but it could also lead to catastrophic outcomes if misaligned AI (AI acting against humanity's shared values) schemes to subvert controls while building its successors. AI 2027 offers one example. In its "race" ending, Agent-4, a superhuman AI researcher with its own vision of Earth as a scientific masterpiece, designs its successor, Agent-5, to be aligned to Agent-4 rather than to humans. Agent-5, with far more intelligence and power, helps take control away from humanity.

​The leading AI companies are racing to develop superintelligence: systems more powerful than all of humanity. Renowned AI researchers such as Yoshua Bengio, the world's most-cited scientist, and Geoffrey Hinton, Nobel laureate in physics, have warned for years about the risk of human extinction from artificial intelligence and are calling for a ban on the development of superintelligence. ​Eight billion people never agreed to this! ​And it is moving faster than previously assumed: at Anthropic, one of these companies, the pace of AI progress has roughly doubled within a year. This was reported on 5 November by the independent research organisation METR. The main reason, according to METR: AI now helps very effectively to build the next AI. This could be the beginning of a cascade of rapid advances that ends in an irreversible loss of control. ​METR was not allowed to publish the most informative evidence: Anthropic had it redacted from the final report. According to METR, precisely this evidence indicates that the pace could be even more than twice as high and is still rising.

We need commitments for 25% compute for safety by 205 ECI points, progressively increasing with further capabilities. (Or at least push for governmental pressure on companies to do so.) Or, rather, we need specific, middle-ground commitments with concrete demands and conditions that are triggered. The example proposed is not random and also, obviously, not enough: asking for 25% compute for safety on the eve of TED-AI - estimated by AI Futures Model to be 210 - seems like a bad joke compared to the demands from compute-based plans like How to Pace the AI Frontier or Pacing AI via Compute Reallocation, which often asked for research compute to be limited to <20%. But it is something that, IMO, can happen and can set important institutional precedents that serve to prepare for a more sophisticated pause. Why I chose 25% compute by 205 ECI: Nuclear plants often have 20-30% at the lower bound of their capital costs going into safety protocols and procedures. Source, Source (look at Appendix 1 - Hitachi 3b). I pick a midpoint of 25%.

### Why everyone should be doing therapy
Source: Big Think

Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · baseline

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Big Think [public_ideas] https://bigthink.com/mini-philosophy/why-everyone-should-be-doing-therapy/

I would bet my house that you’re living with something. There is some sickness, pain, or condition you’ve learned to deal with. Because there is no such thing as “perfect” health. Everyone you talk to, everyone you see on the street, everyone in the line at the coffee shop, has something they have to adapt to. It might be something mild, like dry skin in the winter or being nearsighted. It might be a chronically bad back or intermittent migraines. Or, it might be something that requires more of us: diabetes tests, dialysis, the latest cancer treatment. Everyone, everywhere, is dealing with something. Mental health is no different. I’m sometimes asked if I’m an anxious or obsessive person, and my reply is almost always the same. Yes, I can certainly feel anxious, and yes, I can display obsessive behaviors, but am I anxious or obsessive? I don’t think so. I am the way I am, and I have learned how to live with that. We all grow to deal with the world as best we can. I have strategies, tools, and ways of thinking that allow me to operate in the world, and I’m sure you do as well.

Attribution: LessWrong [public_ideas] https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/emigsbmpWiJxRkDvw/frontier-clock-tracking-the-us-china-ai-gap

Since DeepSeek R1 came out, many people have felt that Chinese models are catching up to the US frontier. Using a new benchmark, Frontier Clock, I find the opposite: while noisy, the US-China gap has grown by around 2.4 months per year. Inspired by Epoch AI's “Chinese AI models have lagged the US frontier by 7 months on average since 2023” and Parv Mahajan's “The US-China AI gap is very uncertain,” I built an AI benchmark that measures the gaps between the US, China, non-China open weights, and individual labs. Instead of giving each model a traditional benchmark score, Frontier Clock assigns a “frontier-equivalent date”: the date when the world’s best publicly released model first had the same capability level as that model. It uses Epoch AI’s ECI benchmark data. The “Method” section in frontierclock.org discusses how the data is used. This graph from the website plots each model’s frontier-equivalent date on the y-axis and release date on the x-axis: Frontier Clock classifies models into three groups: “US Closed,” “China,” and “Open weights (non-China).

Rohan Subramani Something I posted on LW about a month ago that I’d like to discuss with people here, because it feels pretty cruxy for threat modeling imo: How do people feel about the following 3 claims? We currently have AIs that try to do a reasonable balance of what their developers and users intend on the vast majority of inputs they will see in practice (eg, practically useful tasks or fun tasks that people ask for work or personal use). We’re on track for that to remain true through to early superintelligences. (Skip if you don’t agree with 1.) AI x-risk from misalignment is >10% likely even if we only ever build AIs that do a reasonable balance of what their developers and users intend on the vast majority of inputs (because of the misaligned behavior on the tiny minority of inputs).

There are a few questions that humanity has always pondered, yet scarcely could satisfactorily answer until the proper scientific advances came along. Questions like: What is the Universe? Where did it come from? How did it get to be this way? And what is its ultimate fate? These are questions that have been with us since time immemorial, yet remained unanswerable for nearly all of human history. Beginning in the 20th century and now into the 21st century, many of these questions are finally getting comprehensive answers thanks to incredible advances in physics and astronomy. However, perhaps the biggest question of all — the question of “Are we alone in the Universe?” — remains as perhaps the greatest existential unanswered question of all. While the current generation of ground-based and space-based telescopes can take us far into the Universe, this is a question that’s currently the reach of any observatory that presently exists.

Years ago on the way to New Zealand for my doctoral studies, I stopped in Los Angeles to visit a friend. He organized a trip to Joshua Tree, where we hiked and camped. Come nightfall, I gazed at the stars and clouds — or so I thought. My friend pointed out that the cloudcover was, in fact, the Milky Way. I didn’t realize our galaxy was ever visible to the naked eye, and I was deeply moved. The vast stillness of the desert, the free-roaming coyotes and the thick blanket of stars reminded me that we humans are only a tiny part of it all, yet also unbreakably connected to this stretching, expansive universe. More than a decade later, the awe of that experience remains important and vivid in my life. Panoramic view of the Milky Way arch over Joshua trees in the Mojave Desert. Viktor Skalican / Alamy Now, as a psychological scientist, I study awe for a living. Last summer, my colleagues and I asked 200 people in the UK to document their encounters with awe over six weeks.

### How Voyager 1 became the first spacecraft to reach one light-day
Source: Big Think
Published: 2026-11-18 07:00 UTC
URL: https://bigthink.com/starts-with-a-bang/voyager-1-one-light-day/
Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-20 01:35 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Big Think [public_ideas] https://bigthink.com/starts-with-a-bang/voyager-1-one-light-day/

As of November 18, 2026, if you send a signal out at the speed of light in the direction of Voyager 1 — humanity’s most distant spacecraft — it will now take more than a full day for that signal to arrive. At that impressive distance, more than three times the distance to Pluto, over 16 billion miles, and over 25.9 billion kilometers away, the Sun appears 30,000 times fainter than it does from Earth. (That’s still brighter than the full Moon, but only by a factor of 14, or under three astronomical magnitudes.) It’s moving away from the Sun at a current speed of 60,770 km/hr (37,760 mph), and has reached that one light-day milestone after a cumulative journey of 49 years and 72 days. In all the years since 1977, we’ve never launched another spacecraft that has rivaled Voyager 1. No other spacecraft has traveled as far; no other spacecraft is leaving the Solar System with as rapid a velocity; no current or even planned spacecraft is on track to ever overtake it.

Psychiatrist Iain McGilchrist has spent 35 years studying how the brain shapes consciousness. In this full interview, he explains why the two hemispheres attend to the world in radically different ways, and how one narrow, grasping mode has come to dominate Western civilization. He then explores the nature of reality: a creative cosmos that flows at the edge of chaos, where consciousness is primary and matter is one of its phases. He closes with what makes a human life flourish. This video How to navigate the world with two halves of one brain is featured on Big Think.

In this episode, the conversation explores Rodrigo Sorogoyen and Diego Luna’s earliest cinematic experiences and how trust and a sense of togetherness form the foundation of their approach to working with actors. Rodrigo Sorogoyen is a Spanish director and screenwriter whose work spans nearly twenty feature films, series and short films. His filmography moves between intricate narratives rooted in political and crime thrillers, and deeply intimate and socially driven dramas. His 2017 short film Madre was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Live Action Short Film and later became the starting point for a 2019 feature-length adaptation, which premiered in the Orizzonti section of the Venice Film Festival. In 2022, he presented The Beasts at the Cannes Film Festival, earning the César Award for Best Foreign Film, Goya Awards for Best Director and Best Original Screenplay, and the San Sebastián Film Festival Audience Award. He also co-wrote and co-directed the romantic series The New Years (2024).

With his award-winning movie Holy Spider (2022), writer/director Ali Abassi experienced the complexities and dangers of trying to make movies in repressive Iran…but he also says “the most challenging thing I’ve ever done” was making his Oscar-nominated The Apprentice (2024), about a young Donald J. Trump. Abassi tells host Rico Gagliano about both, and what it was like to navigate two very different kinds of censorship. The MUBI Podcast returns for its 12th season, “Under Pressure.” At a time when artists worldwide are being threatened or stifled by their governments, host Rico Gagliano tells the stories of filmmakers from across history and around the world who have made movies in spite of incredible state pressure to compromise, give in, or give up. From 1970s Turkey to modern-day America, these are alternately wild, sobering, controversial, and inspiring tales of art by any means necessary. The Last Emperor (Bernardo Bertolucci, 1987). When Jeremy Thomas died on September 11, 2026, the British film industry lost a titan. A producer who paid no heed to the vagaries of popular culture, Thomas was led by his impeccable palate for cinematic ambition, unswayed by whether audiences or critics came along for the ride. A list of filmmakers whose work makes up Thomas’s production portfolio reads like a who’s who of maverick visionaries, each of them fiercely loyal to the last: Nicolas Roeg and David Cronenberg; Takeshi Kitano and Jonathan Glazer; Nagisa Ōshima and Wim Wenders; Jerzy Skolimowski and Bernardo Bertolucci, whose The Last Emperor (1987) won Thomas the Academy Award for Best Picture. Cinema ran through Thomas’s veins. Both his father and uncle were filmmakers, respectively behind the uniquely British series of Doctor (1954–70) and Carry On (1958–92) films, and Thomas spent much of his youth on the sound stages at Pinewood Studios.

Attribution: MUBI Notebook [film_moving_image] https://mubi.com/en/notebook/posts/scene-report-summer-break-in-mexico-city

Scene Report is a series that explores a city's moviegoing culture over a month. Illustration by Angelo Dolojan. There are summers when Mexico City belongs to cinema. This was not one of them—it belonged to football. Months before the first whistle, sidewalks were being repaired with unusual urgency, facades were being repainted, metro stations acquired new signage, long-neglected public spaces suddenly became worthy of investment. Like every global mega-event, the FIFA World Cup arrived with the familiar rhetoric of urban renewal and international prestige. Whether those promises will outlast the tournament remains to be seen. What mattered during those weeks was that the city had accepted football as its temporary organizing principle. As someone who had deliberately decided to stay in Mexico City to experience the tournament, I surrendered without resistance. I have always loved football, and the chance to watch a World Cup unfold in my own city felt like a once-in-a-lifetime experience. During the tournament, everyday routines dissolved into celebration.

In this month’s antidote to the algorithm, Juliet Jacques explores the playful and experimental soundtracks to games on the popular tape-based home computer I spent my first year at the University of Manchester in halls of residence. They put me in with a group of lads who were really into techno, and drum and bass – a challenge to my sensibilities, as I had a tribal allegiance to punk, post-punk and independent music. During our first weeks together, in September 2000, a single came out that instantly became a massive hit but united my flatmates in disgust: ‘Kernkraft 400’ by Zombie Nation. I immediately recognised the hook – “it’s from a Commodore 64 game”, I told them. “I bet it fucking... The post Organic Intelligence LXII: C64 Game Soundtracks appeared first on The Quietus.

To accompany his Unlimited Editions report in The Wire 514, Tim Fish compiles an annotated playlist of tracks from the Liverpool label When Blah Records emerged into the UK’s hiphop landscape in 2006, they formed part of an alternative movement to a rather dominant London scene. Co-founded by Lee Scott and Alex Jennings (aka Molotov), the label was primarily a way to officially distribute music for the rap crew Children Of The Damned (COTD), and the majority of artists who have put out records on the label over the subsequent 20 years have all had some real-life connection to Scott. The following playlist outlines some of Blah's most significant records. Children Of The Damned “Cold Sag Run Marathon” From Brick Pelican (2009) Children Of The Damned were the original Blah artists and they still remain at the core of the label today, albeit with expanded numbers and a slightly different name. This track gives a flavour of their origins and an even better indicator of how much their sound has evolved.

Mark Korven’s scores for The Black Phone (2021) and Them (2021) destabilise hermetic soundworlds to convey psychological violence, writes Philip Brophy in his latest Secret History of Film Music column The contribution of Canadian composer Mark Korven to contemporary horror cinema is aligned with composers who sculpt their scores through tactile manipulation. His self-built Apprehension Engine, a hybrid guitar-percussion instrument, empowers distinctive acoustic control. Korven commissioned Toronto based guitar maker Tony Duggan-Smith to build the modest box incorporating tools and techniques favoured by Korven: a hurdy-gurdy for cranking, a spring reverb for metallic resonance, metal rods and wooden tongues for bowing (similar to the waterphone), and a stretched wire for E-bowing. Its abject sonics pepper Robert Eggers’s The Lighthouse (2019) with terse shudders and emotional spikes, and are also audible in Adam Schindler and Brian Netto’s Don’t Move (2024).

To accompany his Global Ear feature in The Wire 514, Simon Coates compiles an annotated playlist of tracks from the Sri Lankan city Situated on Colombo’s Vauxhall Street, Musicmatters sits at the centre of the Sri Lankan city's experimental music world. “A lot of my introduction to experimentation in music came through Musicmatters around 2010,” says bass player Uvindu Perera. “I was new to it then, but these people were already listening widely and sharing references.” Simultaneously a collective, a school (Perera now teaches there), a record label and home to the Sound Room performance space, Musicmatters offers both an alternative to exam-heavy Western music education and provides space for explorations in sound as art and experimentation. Many of the musicians in this playlist have links to the organisation. Isuru Kumarasinghe “Time #1” From Ekāgra: Sitting With Trees Under Skies (Bandcamp) 2020 “Time #1” is taken from the 2020 album, Ekāgra: Sitting With Trees Under Skies, that formed the soundtrack to a video artwork Isuru Kumarasinghe made during the Covid lockdowns.

Watch an exclusive clip of Turkish improv band ZeN’s Bakırköy Psychiatric Hospital concert from 1998 On 23 June 1998, Istanbul based experimental rock group ZeN performed at Bakırköy Psychiatric Hospital, following an invitation from two nurses who worked there. The musicians visited the hospital beforehand and decided to approach the performance with sensitivity to their audience while remaining true to their commitment to improvisation. At times, the lyrics seem to tell the story of the hospital and the concert itself, responding directly to the surroundings. The performance subsequently became one of the group’s most remarkable and cult recordings, released on cassette and CD in 1999 and reissued on vinyl in 2023. This exclusive edit with English subtitles is hosted by The Wire ahead of the release of a new documentary, ZeNistan, exploring the activities of ZeN throughout the 1990s.

### Against the Grain: Music criticism can become critical again – here's how
Source: The Wire Magazine
Published: 2026-11-09 00:00 UTC
URL: https://www.thewire.co.uk/in-writing/collateral-damage/against-the-grain-music-criticism-can-become-critical-again-here-s-how
Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · culture_probe
Fetched: 2026-11-20 01:35 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Wire Magazine [music_sound] https://www.thewire.co.uk/in-writing/collateral-damage/against-the-grain-music-criticism-can-become-critical-again-here-s-how

Popular music criticism can become relevant again by situating itself in broader theoretical frameworks, argues Rafael Lubner in The Wire 514 These are lean times for popular music criticism. Negotiating a gutted publishing landscape, amid a Spotify-led devaluation of listening, the form finds itself under serious threat. One index of criticism’s attenuated state is the narrowing frame of reference employed by critics to apprehend musical objects – rarely do we find new works in the visual arts, film or literature employed to understand transformations in music’s sound or form. Take, as a point of comparison, Greg Tate’s recently reissued Flyboy In The Buttermilk (reviewed in The Wire 513). Here are passionate defences of Miles Davis’s earth-shaking mid-1970s funk odysseys alongside surveys of Afrodiasporic art and reviews of writer Nathaniel Mackey and literary critic Henry Louis Gates Jr. Contemporary music criticism, by contrast, seems resolutely committed to understanding music as siloed from the non-musical.

Barra Peñasco is a high-end bar inside the Rosewood Mandarina Hotel in the Riviera Nayarit. Perched on a cliffside between the canopy of white fig trees and palms, it faces the Pacific Ocean. The project responds to the site's unique conditions through an open architecture that accompanies different moments of hospitality: arriving, taking a seat, sharing a drink, and lingering as the sunset transforms the horizon and music extends the experience into the night. Its mixology menu, inspired by the four elements and Náyeri and Wixárika traditions, dialogues with this natural setting.

Source: Rock Paper Shotgun
Published: 2026-11-19 15:00 UTC
URL: https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/remembering-the-back-alley-brawls-of-the-warriors-a-rockstar-city-game-that-isnt-an-open-world

Attribution: Rock Paper Shotgun [games] https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/remembering-the-back-alley-brawls-of-the-warriors-a-rockstar-city-game-that-isnt-an-open-world

The older I get, the more fascinated I somehow become by how videogames depict night, how particular technologies at particular times give rise to particular nightlives. I've already gushed about the Starlight Zone in Sonic the Hedgehog – the mild dissociation incubated by the soft, ceaseless glare of the construction yard, the eyeless brick at the level's nadir, the sleepless glitter of the skyline. Now, let me wind the clock forward, and backward, to Rockstar Toronto's The Warriors. One long night from the late '70s, sweaty and electric and menacing, fed through dank and sullen polygons from 2005. Probably the best move Rockstar made with their adaptation of Walter Hill's film is to retain the element of phantasmagoria. Both the game and the movie open with a view of Coney Island's Wonder Wheel, its neon lamps forming a floating tracery of Morse code, cabins swinging almost imperceptibly against solid darkness. This is a kind of night in which light is more emblem than illumination, refusing to travel far, clinging to its source like a frightened ghost. Read more

### Handheld Raman spectroscopy for ex vivo molecular assessment of cervical lesions: A methodological feasibility study
Source: PLOS ONE Biology
Published: 2026-11-19 14:00 UTC
URL: https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0363469
Source meta: journal · primary · R4 · P4 · signal
Updated: 2026-11-19 14:00 UTC
Fetched: 2026-11-20 01:36 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: PLOS ONE Biology [academic_research] https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0363469

by Yixuan Zhang, Huan Wang, Ying He, Siyuan Zhang, Pengyu Wang, Yimin Han Current diagnostic workflows for cervical lesions remain constrained by processing time, sampling representativeness, and limited molecular-level tissue assessment. Handheld Raman spectroscopy may provide label-free molecular profiling of ex vivo tissue specimens. In this methodological feasibility study, we evaluated a defined ex vivo acquisition workflow using a handheld 785-nm Raman spectrometer. We systematically evaluated laser power, integration time, and tissue thickness, and 128 mW laser power, 4000 ms integration time, and approximately 1-mm-thick tissue sections were selected as the working acquisition conditions for subsequent cervical measurements. The cervical cohort comprised 74 patients contributing 212 Raman spectra and was evaluated for two predefined primary binary classification tasks: invasive cervical cancer versus noncancer lesions (B1) and high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) versus benign lesions plus low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) (B2).

by Qiong Zhou, Changxian Xiong, Linshu Wang, Huai Pang, Rucong Liu, Jingkun Yi, Yu Han, Yuan Zhou Inter-tissue/organ communication (ITC) is essential for coordinating metabolism, immunity, development and disease progression. However, experimentally supported ITC events are dispersed across individual studies, hindering a systematic retrieval of their molecular mediators, source-to-target tissue routes and supporting evidence. Here, we present IntiCom-DB v2.0, an updated literature-derived database of experimentally supported ITC events. Compared with the previous version, IntiCom-DB v2.0 expands the curated collection to 1,862 entries from 1,485 publications, covering 651 unique ITC molecules across proteins, RNAs and metabolites. The updated database identifies 398 distinct communication routes between 51 source tissues and 53 target tissues, with protein-mediated events representing the largest category. To facilitate the functional interpretation of ITC-mediating proteins, IntiCom-DB v2.

by Ming Sun, Yanyan Liu, Baoyi Lu, Mingshuo Wang, Pingxin Liu Spent mushroom substrate (SMS) and pig manure (PM) represent two dominant types of agricultural organic waste. Co-composting of these two substrates at extreme mixing ratios—common in regions with a surplus of a single waste type—frequently suffers from C/N imbalance, suppressed humification, and substantial nutrient loss. Maillard reaction precursors (MRPs) are well-documented key regulators of humus (HS) formation, yet their regulatory mechanisms and efficacy in SMS–PM co-composting at extreme mixing ratios remain poorly understood. In this study, we performed a 120-day aerobic solid-state incubation experiment using two extreme SMS: PM mass ratios (9:1 for the high-SMS system, 1:9 for the high-PM system), with catechol (Cat), glucose (Glu), and glycine (Gly) applied as exogenous MRPs. The results demonstrated that all three MRPs significantly improved compost maturity, nutrient retention, and HS synthesis relative to the unamended control. Glu accelerated phytotoxin degradation, increased GI by 26.8%–45.

by Seung-Hun Lee The 2025 World Aquatics rule revisions for water polo aimed to accelerate offensive tempo and alter tactical decision-making by reducing the field length, shot clock duration, and possession reset times. This study used the 2024 and 2025 Men’s Water Polo World Championships as consecutive editions of the same elite international competition to provide an initial quasi-experimental assessment of performance changes associated with these revisions. Performance indicators across four domains (offensive performance, goalkeeping, exclusions, and game management) were analyzed using a multivariate analysis of variance. Notably, significant multivariate differences were observed between tournaments across all performance domains. Subsequent univariate analyses showed that these differences were primarily reflected in the frequency and distribution of match events. Most shooting and save rates showed no statistically significant difference between tournaments.

arXiv:2611.23319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI now produces machine-checked mathematics faster than researchers can read it. Can such theorems do practical computational work? We reuse one from \mbox{OpenAI's} Lean~4 relativistic Vlasov--Maxwell library: initial fields determine the field at an outside point until plasma signals reach it, and the energy leaving a surrounding box before they reach its faces. New Lean proofs and numerical bounds give particle-free references for particle-in-cell simulations across three tasks. Domain size follows analytically from observation time, exposing boundary and initialization errors in WarpX and Smilei that global energy checks missed. Grid choice can be tested directly: combining two coarse grids recovers unknown plasma inputs within tolerance at a median 14.9-fold speedup over a fine grid, where the medium grid alone fails. For reduced models, the bounds establish the minimum number of time curves needed to predict energy loss.

arXiv:2611.23340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The physical origin of cosmic acceleration remains one of the central unresolved problems of modern cosmology. Although the $\Lambda$CDM model successfully describes a wide range of cosmological observations, its interpretation in terms of a strictly constant vacuum energy faces long-standing theoretical challenges, motivating the search for physically grounded alternatives. In this work, we develop a thermodynamic parametrization of dark energy (TPDE) by combining the second law of thermodynamics with the kinematic evolution of the Universe. By imposing physically motivated constraints on the cosmic deceleration parameter and reconstructing its evolution through a Pad\'e approximant, we derive a one-parameter extension of $\Lambda$CDM in which late-time accelerated expansion emerges from thermodynamic principles rather than an assumed cosmological constant.

arXiv:2611.23412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Disruptions in high-current tokamaks, such as ARC, may result in megaampere-scale runaway electron currents. In this work, we evaluate mitigation strategies via massive material injection, accounting for the combined impact of scrape-off losses due to vertical displacement events and current profile relaxation during the thermal quench. We find that scrape-off losses alone yield only modest reductions in runaway electron currents, but combining them with current flattening creates a beneficial synergistic effect. The latter broadens the current channel outward, shifting efficient runaway electron generation closer to the plasma edge where the dynamically contracting boundary can effectively scrape off the electron beams. This interplay significantly expands the operational window for mitigation toward lower assimilated densities, theoretically reducing runaway currents to manageable levels at experimentally feasible assimilated quantities.

arXiv:2611.23429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a critical component of the climate system. Climate models have long predicted a slowing of the AMOC due to anthropogenic forcing, with a risk of passing tipping points in the future. The question of whether the AMOC is already weakening is still somewhat controversial. Continuous monitoring is only available for the past two decades, a period too short to tease apart contributions of natural variability and climate change. Reconstructions of AMOC strength going back further in time have different limitations which are debated in the literature. Here we compile and discuss this heterogeneous body of evidence, focusing on latitudes south of 45{\deg}N where northward and southward flow are separated vertically. We conclude that the balance of multiple lines of evidence strongly supports a past and ongoing AMOC slowing in response to global warming, although some uncertainty remains regarding its magnitude and timing.

arXiv:2611.23449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore a dynamic vacuum energy scenario within the Weyl Integrable Spacetime (WIS) framework and provide the Friedmann--Lema\^itre (FL) cosmology equations under a metric endowed with a lapse function. We pay particular attention to the implications of inflationary dynamics. We show that the explicit vacuum decay source cancels in the FL acceleration equation, where the Hubble slow-roll parameter is controlled by the non-vacuum sector alone, while the dynamic vacuum defined in proper time $\Lambda(\tau)$ itself continues to enter the observables through the expansion rate. We identify the warm inflation (WI) dissipation coefficient with one half of the logarithmic decay rate of the vacuum energy, $\Upsilon=-\tfrac{1}{2} d\ln\Lambda/d\tau$, hence the phenomenological friction coefficient is tied to the vacuum sector rather than computed from explicit inflaton--bath microphysics.

arXiv:2611.23457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) is a next-generation facility expected to address fundamental open questions in nuclear physics, including the structure and dynamics of gluons in nucleons and nuclei. The Barrel Imaging Calorimeter (BIC) is the electromagnetic calorimeter of the ePIC detector, designed to meet the stringent performance requirements of the EIC, providing precise measurements and particle identification of scattered electrons, photons, and neutral mesons. The BIC is a high-granularity sampling calorimeter based on lead absorbers interleaved with scintillating fibers, complemented by pixelated imaging layers based on the AstroPix monolithic active pixel sensor. This hybrid design enables both accurate energy and position measurements, as well as three-dimensional shower reconstruction, making it a key component for realizing the full physics potential of the EIC. The BIC has successfully completed its Preliminary Design Review last year and is currently progressing toward the Final Design Review.

Although Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's victory in Brazil's presidential election promises executive commitment to science, public health, and environmental protection, the political reality signals a serious governability crisis. The unprecedented conservative surge in the 2026 legislative elections created a deeply hostile Congress, leaving a divided nation in which evidence-based governance, public health systems, and ecological preservation face imminent institutional gridlock. This political split, reflected in the 51·79% to 48·21% election result,1 is heightened by memories of past anti-democratic actions following the 2022 election, including civilian encampments outside military installations, demands for military intervention, and the January 2023 storming of Brasília's democratic institutions.

Source: The Lancet
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01500-X/fulltext?rss=yes
Source meta: journal · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Updated: 2026-10-29 23:30 UTC

Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Lancet [academic_research] https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01500-X/fulltext?rss=yes

Irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea are disorders of gut–brain interaction, the symptoms of which include abnormal stool consistency or frequency accompanied by varying degrees of abdominal pain, discomfort, bloating, or distension. These conditions affect 20% of the global population with a relapsing and remitting course. Risk factors include female sex, younger age, a history of common mental disorders, and acute enteric infection. The pathophysiology of irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea remain incompletely understood, but are thought to be secondary to aberrant interactions throughout the gut–brain axis, resulting in disordered gut motility and visceral hypersensitivity.

Among the awardees is Prof. Anton Wallner from the Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf (HZDR), whose project SUPREME attempts to reconstruct the history of nearby cosmic explosions over the past 500 million years and shed light on how nature creates its heaviest elements.

The Simons Observatory is online and surveying the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) in greater detail than ever before. It's looking for tiny fluctuations in the CMB caused by primordial gravitational waves. These waves, if detected, would be as close to slam-dunk evidence for the Big Bang that we can expect to find.

AI agents can generate code at a scale that’s hard for humans to review line-by-line. PDD Kit helps ensure the code is doing what the developer intended by creating formal specifications and testing against them. It converts developer intent into a Verus specification, proves AI-generated code meets it for every input, and uses tests where proofs aren't practical. Developers review intent, not every line. Anonymous Coward writes: Microsoft's recent global Microsoft 365 outage has highlighted how much businesses, schools and organisations depend on a small number of cloud providers for essential communication and daily operations. The disruption affected services including Outlook, Exchange Online and Microsoft Teams, leaving users unable to access tools they rely on for work and communication. Beyond the immediate disruption, the incident raises a bigger technology question: how prepared are organisations when a major cloud provider experiences a widespread failure? Cloud computing offers convenience, scalability and lower infrastructure costs, but heavy dependence on a single provider can create significant operational risks. Businesses need to consider backup communication systems, disaster recovery plans and ways to maintain essential operations when their primary services become unavailable.

### PostgreSQL 19 Released
Source: Simon Willison's Weblog
Published: 2026-11-19 20:43 UTC
URL: https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/19/postgresql-19/
Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Updated: 2026-11-19 20:43 UTC
Fetched: 2026-11-20 01:36 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Simon Willison's Weblog [computing_cultures] https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/19/postgresql-19/

PostgreSQL 19 Released Most years PostgreSQL ships a new release in September, but this year's release came two months later thanks mainly to the flurry of issues that the PostgreSQL team needed to address as part of the ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse. This release was definitely worth the wait. My favorite new feature is this one: For applications that send reads to standbys, PostgreSQL 19 adds "read-your-writes" consistency with the new WAIT FOR LSN command. A session on a standby can use WAIT FOR LSN to wait until the standby has replayed the write-ahead log (WAL) up to a specific log sequence number (LSN) before running a query, so the application can read data it just wrote on the primary. In practice, that looks like this: UPDATE movie SET genre = 'Dramatic' WHERE genre = 'Drama'; SELECT pg_current_wal_insert_lsn(); That returns a value like 0/0306EE20. Store that somewhere (a signed cookie would work) such that on a subsequent request your application can do: WAIT FOR LSN '0/0306EE20' WITH (TIMEOUT '0.

### [$] Added indirection allows for larger BPF programs
Source: LWN.net
Published: 2026-11-19 17:32 UTC
URL: https://lwn.net/Articles/1106537/
Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-20 01:36 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: LWN.net [computing_cultures] https://lwn.net/Articles/1106537/

The BPF verifier has historically worked by tracing every possible path of execution through a program, checking, at each instruction, that various safety properties hold. This works, but it can result in an exponential increase in the number of states that need checking in programs with complicated control-flow. Alexei Starovoitov, one of the kernel's core BPF maintainers, has shared a patch set that substantially reworks how the verifier tracks states, in order to reduce the size of that exponential explosion.

"Arthur T Knackerbracket" writes: https://www.theregister.com/research/2026/11/16/google-ai-agent-turned-a-security-patch-into-a-working-exploit-with-no-human-help/5309926 A suspected Russian-speaking operator used an AI agent to turn security patches into working exploits with no human in the loop – a first such occurrence, according to the Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) – before ultimately stealing data from victim organizations. Google documented this attack in its fourth-quarter 2026 AI threat tracker, and said it marks a significant advance in how attackers use LLMs for fully autonomous vulnerability discovery and exploitation compared to Q3. In this case, the threat hunters found an exposed staging server hosting a multi-agent vulnerability research and weaponization framework that integrates with multiple frontier and local models. The framework, called exploit_agent, used Russian-language tooling, and was configured to conduct continuous differential analysis of "popular web application software," according to the report.

PiMuNu writes: This report presents the results of research into several different methods to power the climbers on the space elevator. The first part of the report states the requirements common to any climber power system and establishes the power requirements for multiple climbers on the tether simultaneously. https://www.isec.org/2026-study The power delivery methods shown are laser power beaming, microwave power beaming, solar-powered climbers, and climbers powered by an electrically conducting tether that is energized. The short wavelength of the laser-powered climbers allows for the smallest, lightest receivers on the climbers. Laser systems do not have the efficiency of microwave-powered systems, but the longer microwave wavelength leads to a rapidly diverging beam that forces the receivers on the climber to be very large for microwave systems. Microwave power beaming may also be limited to a maximum power density in the ionosphere of 230 W/m2 to avoid communications disruptions. Further work is needed to determine the appropriate power density limit.

hubie writes: School of Business marketing professor Suzanne Makarem says physician-influencers may carry more impact than a follower's own doctor, and 'that should give us pause': Young adults following physicians on TikTok consider them more accessible, credible and altruistic than their own doctors, even when the physician-influencers are selling products. Moreover, the followers haven't actually confirmed the influencers' medical credentials. Those are the main findings of a new study from Virginia Commonwealth University, co-authored by Suzanne Makarem, Ph.D., and published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs. "Young consumers are usually very literate when it comes to social media influencers and commercial intent. But when you have a physician on TikTok, that becomes something different," said Makarem, an associate professor of marketing in VCU's School of Business. "We're already trained to respond positively to credentialed experts. Now we're seeing them as 'these doctors who have busy lives and already make a lot of money – ­they don't have to be doing this.

remote_worker writes: A look at the difference in effort, understanding, and recall between creating something versus verifying it, and the human tendencies towards verifying things. https://theconversation.com/catching-ais-mistakes-is-a-mental-burden-and-a-drag-on-productivity-291748 By now, almost everyone has asked an AI agent a question, only to realize that the answer seems not quite right. Something might be missing or wrong or out of date. An executive assistant told me she uses AI tools for drafting itineraries and briefings, but she's caught enough issues that she now builds time into her workflow to thoroughly check for inaccuracies and biases. Therein lies the catch: AI responses can improve productivity, but the gains are often countered by time and mental energy spent determining whether the output is accurate and appropriate. This is the verification burden. Sometimes the cost is worth it, sometimes it isn't. Original Submission Read more of this story at SoylentNews.

Release: datasette-arrows 0.1a0 Datasette 1.0a43 added the ability for plugins to implement streaming export formats. Datasette core supports streaming CSV and TSV - you can export millions of lines of data from a table without needing to load it all into memory, because those two file formats support streaming data in chunks. The register_output_renderer() plugin hook can now be used to implement the same pattern for other formats. I've learned never to release a new plugin feature without accompanying it with a plugin that uses it. Claude Fable 5.2 suggested the Apache Arrow streaming format as a good option, and built this plugin in almost a single shot. Add the plugin to Datasette (datasette install datasette-arrows) and the export dialog gains this new Arrow option: This screenshot is from Datasette's main branch - the most recent release doesn't yet group streaming formats such as Arrow with the TSV and CSV in the "All rows in this table" section, but that's coming in the next alpha release. Data contracts are a way to describe the contents and guarantees of datasets. Simon Harrer and Arif Wider describe in detail what they are and how to use them. They apply practices from API design to data by treating them as data-providing services - such as data products - whose interfaces we want to define as clearly as possible. This approach significantly increases the robustness of large-scale data landscapes, and gives both people and AI agents the explicit, trustworthy metadata they need to work with data autonomously, which is why more and more enterprises are adopting them. more…

External sandboxes for coding agents I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code that is executed by agents, with a focus on making it safer to try out local models without worrying that a mistake or prompt injection attack might cause them to take damaging actions on a machine. I worked on this project with Prime Radiant, the AI research lab behind Superpowers and other projects. My post on the Prime Radiant blog introduces the external sandbox pattern, where code executed by the agent runs inside a dedicated sandbox while the agent itself lives outside of that sandbox. To demonstrate this pattern we've released three sandbox server implementations: external-sandbox-v86 runs a Node.js server which then uses v86 to run Alpine Linux inside WebAssembly. external-sandbox-container is a Python web server which runs the sandbox in Alpine Linux inside an Apple Containers instance. external-sandbox-quicksand is another Python web server, this time using Microsoft's Quicksand sandboxing library, which bundles QEMU and Alpine Linux in a Python package!

Distributed systems are hard to test because partial failures overlap with live traffic and the same fault can produce different execution traces on different runs. Unmesh Joshi describes how deterministic simulation testing addresses this by replacing real clocks, networks, and storage with simulated components driven by a single-threaded execution loop. This allows simulating both hard failures and routine slowdowns—such as network and disk latency spikes—and more importantly makes every execution reproducible. This article explains the technique using a quorum key-value store as a running example, with code from Tickloom, a Java implementation of the approach. more…

### Bliki: Generated Glossary
Source: Martin Fowler
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://martinfowler.com/bliki/GeneratedGlossary.html
Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R5 · P5 · baseline
Updated: 2026-11-12 14:15 UTC
Fetched: 2026-11-20 01:36 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Martin Fowler [computing_cultures] https://martinfowler.com/bliki/GeneratedGlossary.html

When we use LLMs in a specialized domain, such as the operations of any reasonably-large organization, there is a lot of specialized vocabulary. Such words and specialized meanings will be foreign to an LLM because they aren't in its training set, making it harder for the LLM to be effective when doing tasks in that domain. One technique to aid this is to use an LLM to generate a glossary of the terminology in that domain, and make this glossary available for any LLMs doing work in those circumstances. The sources for the LLM can be any material within the organization concerned such as documents, emails, and chat logs. In some cases getting transcripts of audio or video may be helpful, although most organizations generate enough text to do the job. The glossary-generating LLM should look for single words, and phrases of several words that regularly hang out together to form a meaningful term. The generator should be asked to identify terms that are new to it, but also known terms that are being used in unfamiliar ways. The latter can often cause the most confusion.

Attribution: Martin Fowler [computing_cultures] https://martinfowler.com/articles/tests-as-data.html

Automated testing in the age of AI coding assistants is problematic: when AI agents write both production and test code, developers risk losing the assurance that automated tests protect against functional errors. Matteo Vaccari makes three claims: (1) when AI writes the code, developers become its customers; (2) therefore customer tests, not developer tests, become the primary contract between humans and AI; (3) moving that contract into test data rather than test code makes it easier to protect it from unexpected modifications by coding agents. All of this optimizes for human-readable tests that establish a contract between humans and AI. While in the past DSL parsers and custom test runners were expensive to write and maintain, now AI makes them cheap. more…

It’s that time of the year when the November Thoughtworks Technology Radar appears. Again my colleagues have taken a sweep of the technologies that our teams have used in the field, and pulled together a summary of what’s popped up in the last six months. It’s been a busy half-year, one that again has been dominated by AI, and that’s reflected in the many AI blips on the radar. The mass of blips makes it hard to develop a coherent story around trends, but Chris Ford has done a fine job of the writing the accompanying article on macro trends. One team of passionate people experimenting with agents can make almost anything work. They share a context, a credit card and a mental model. They review each other’s work because they sit together, and they know what to check and how much latitude to give the coding agent. Two hundred people, though, cannot work that way. The moment agentic AI becomes an operating model rather than a pilot, a second layer of problems appears: How is context shared between teams? What’s the token bill? How do we deal with increased review demands?

Long-horizon agents can automate complex tasks that take days or weeks to complete and involve multiple exchanges with people and external systems. Many things can go wrong during this time, including process crashes, network failures, and unanticipated real-world behavior. Kiran Prakash explains durable execution: an emerging pattern that helps agents recover from these failures and move towards their goal. In this programming model, the runtime keeps a record of the result of each step that interacts with the outside world so that, when a failure occurs, the program runs again, completed steps are skipped, and the program's state is rebuilt from the record. more…

Hello! I’ve been working on a Django site recently, and I decided to use SQLite as the database. When I was getting started with using SQLite as database for a website I read a bunch of blog posts about how it is totally fine to use SQLite in production for a small site and I think it is totally fine, but what I did not fully appreciate is that SQLite is still a database, databases are complicated, and I do not know a lot about operating databases. So here are a couple of small things I’ve been learning about running SQLite. This is the 4th website I’ve used SQLite for, and I think this one is harder because with the power of the Django ORM I’ve been making the database do more work than I was previously without Django. I started by turning on WAL mode like all the blog posts said to do and hoping for the best. ANALYZE is apparently important Today I was running a query (using SQLite’s FTS5 for full-text search) on a table with 4000 rows and it took 5 seconds. That seemed wrong to me: computers are fast! It turned out that what I needed to do was to run ANALYZE!
